narrative.overview: Sift should feel like the calm, useful notes a careful diner would want beside a real restaurant menu. Product evidence sits close to the original menu language: a visible phrase, a possible concern, the uncertainty around it, and the question that follows. The system is human and table-side first; AI machinery stays behind the explanation. The website may be more expressive than the app, but it must preserve Sift's protective clarity. Deep teal supplies confidence, true white creates breathing room, and app cream appears primarily inside authentic product surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Real app screens and real menu context carry the visual story.
Editorial scale is used sparingly; the page is not styled like a magazine.
Risk information pairs color with language, hierarchy, and iconography.
Open layouts and strong bands replace repetitive card grids.
Motion explains scanning or state change and always respects reduced motion.

rules.name: The App Cream Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: App cream belongs to Sift's product world. Do not turn it into the website's universal wallpaper.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red appear only when a visible label explains their meaning.

rules.name: The Human First Rule
rules.body: Product and safety explanations use the serif body voice; utility labels use the sans. Technical language never takes over the page.

rules.name: The No Ghost Cards Rule
rules.body: Never combine a decorative 1px border with a wide soft shadow. Choose a structural border or a restrained lift.

dos: Do use authentic current Sift captures as the primary product proof.
Do keep body contrast at or above WCAG 2.2 AA and provide visible keyboard focus.
Do pair every green, amber, or red state with a readable label.
Do use one strong menu-annotation moment as the site's memorable signature.
Do show uncertainty, fallbacks, and limitations beside the reliability method.
Do respect reduced motion and keep interface feedback under 300ms.
donts: Don't use generic AI startup templates: gradient meshes, glowing orbs, AI badges, fake dashboards, invented metrics, or vague intelligence claims.
Don't repeat the V1 website's cream-and-serif editorial template, tiny uppercase kickers, decorative numbered scaffolding, glass navigation, broad shadows, or oversized radii.
Don't add waitlist forms, early-access cards, coming soon calls to action, or launch theater.
Don't present reconstructed, outdated, or invented phone UI as the real product.
Don't claim that a dish is safe to eat, imply a food-safety guarantee, or publish an unsupported accuracy percentage.
Don't fabricate testimonials, press logos, customer counts, or App Store availability.
Don't use gradient text, decorative grid backgrounds, repeating stripes, side-stripe borders, or nested card grids.
